newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close at fourth successive high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close at fourth successive high.

text.p: Australian stocks ended at a record closing high on Tuesday after speculation over a South African takeover of Australia's second largest nickel producer prompted heavy trading in the resources sector.
The All Ordinaries index fell back from an earlier intraday high of 2,695.0 but still managed to set its fourth successive closing record, ending 12.4 points stronger at 2,681.7.
"You've got huge sector buying there," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer from Sydney firm Shaw Stockbroking.
The resources sector was responsible for a brisk day with A$975 million (US$729 million) worth of stocks traded.
Stockbrokers and analysts said rumours abounded in the market that South African mining house Gencor Ltd was poised to make a takeover offer for QNI Ltd.
QNI shares were suspended at the Australian Stock Exchange before Tuesday's opening at the company's request, pending the release of an announcement after a board meeting on Wednesday.
All the major miners traded strongly after the QNI suspension. BHP, Australia's biggest listed company, finished up 40 cents at A$19.30 after almost 5.5 million shares were traded
WMC Ltd was up 28 cents to A$8.50 after 4.8 million shares changed hands and Rio Tinto shares rose 2.6 percent to close at A$23.195.
A weaker Australian dollar, which fell beneath US$0.75, also helped trade in resource stocks, dealers said.

Australian stocks started easier following an overnight downturn on Wall Street and brokers and analysts said the local market would probably revert to its normal slavish following of the Dow Jones Index later in the week.
Over 11 million shares were traded in newspaper house John Fairfax Holdings. Dealers said New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd, a 20 percent stake holder in Fairfax, was the likely buyer.
Commonwealth Bank rose for the second day to close at A$15.19 as investors continued to chase yield stocks. National Australia Bank and Westpac were also up.
